Link.description:
Renders an `<a>` that navigates without a full reload.
Always prefer it over `useNavigate` for anything the user clicks — it stays keyboard- and screen-reader-friendly, and works without JS.

Link with prefetch.description:
Prefetches the route's data and modules.
`intent` fires on hover/focus and is the usual choice; `viewport` suits mobile lists; `render` is eager.

Link with state.description:
Attaches data to the history entry, readable via `useLocation().state`.
Not in the URL — it is lost on reload and cannot be shared.

Link with viewTransition.description:
Wraps the navigation in `document.startViewTransition()`.
Pair with `useViewTransitionState()` to name the morphing elements.

import NavLink.description: Link that knows whether it is active.

NavLink.description:
A `<Link>` that reports `isActive`, `isPending` and `isTransitioning` to its `className`, `style` and children.
Matches by prefix — add `end` so a parent link is not active on child routes.

NavLink end.description: `end` restricts the active state to an exact match — required for a "Home" link pointing at `/`, which otherwise stays active everywhere.

NavLink with pending state.description: `isPending` is true while this link's route is loading — the cheapest per-link loading indicator.

Navigate.description:
Navigates as a side effect of rendering.
In Data or Framework mode prefer `redirect()` in a loader — it runs before rendering and avoids the flash.

Outlet.description: Where a parent route renders its matched child. A layout route without one renders nothing for its children.

Outlet with context.description: Passes data to child routes, read with `useOutletContext()`.

ScrollRestoration.description:
Emulates the browser's scroll restoration for client-side navigation. Render it once, near the root.
Pass `getKey` to share a scroll position across paths.
